durable-harness

durable-harness runs coding-agent harnesses (Pi, OpenCode, libfx's fx, Claude Code and Codex) as durable agents on a [Workflow SDK](https://workflow-sdk.dev) World. Each session is a workflow run: its conversation, the turn in flight and every model and tool call are in the run's event log, so a crash anywhere resumes the turn from the log on another machine, and a tool call that isn't safe to repeat is never run twice. > [!NOTE] > durable-harness is experimental: it's on `0.0.x`, and its API may change > between releases. ## Quick start Install it with a harness, here Pi with [pi-durable](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@earendil-works/pi-durable), in a Next.js app: ```bash npm install durable-harness @earendil-works/pi-durable @earendil-works/chord @earendil-works/pi-ai just-bash ``` Open Pi's own durable `Harness` on a World-backed storage. Agents are tool-less by default; Pi's coding tools go on a virtual workspace, whose files live in the session's log: ```ts // lib/agent.ts import { BACKGROUND_CONTEXT as ctx } from '@earendil-works/chord/context'; import { createRegistry, Harness, type Storage } from '@earendil-works/pi-durable'; import { CodingTools, GATEWAY_PROVIDER, gatewayModels, resumeWith, virtualEnv } from 'durable-harness/pi-durable'; const models = gatewayModels(); const registry = createRegistry(); registry.install(CodingTools); export const agent = { model: { provider: GATEWAY_PROVIDER, modelId: 'anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5' } }; export const open = resumeWith((storage: Storage) => Harness.open(storage, { models, registry, env: virtualEnv() }, ctx)); ``` Serve it from a chat route, and configure the integration: ```ts // app/api/chat/route.ts import { chatRoute } from 'durable-harness/pi-durable'; import { agent, open } from '@/lib/agent'; export const { GET, POST } = chatRoute({ open, agent, authorize: async (request) => { /* your auth */ } }); ``` ```ts // next.config.ts import type { NextConfig } from 'next'; import { withDurableHarness } from 'durable-harness/next'; const nextConfig: NextConfig = { // your existing config }; export default withDurableHarness(nextConfig); ``` `withDurableHarness` discovers modules that export agents created at module scope with `durableAgent`, `claudeCode`, `codex`, `opencode` or `pi`, and modules that register a pi-durable opener with `resumeWith`. A script that creates an agent for itself, an exported factory that creates one later, and code samples in strings or comments are excluded. Import aliases, default exports, export lists, and containers or accessors for an existing agent are supported. For custom factories or effect-only agent registration, list the modules explicitly: `withDurableHarness(nextConfig, { agents: ['lib/agent.ts'] })`. Choose your harness and framework in the [agent harnesses docs](https://vercel.com/docs/agent-harnesses). ## Harnesses - [Pi](https://vercel.com/docs/agent-harnesses/pi): `durable-harness/pi-durable` (recommended: Pi's own durable `Harness` on a World), or `durable-harness/pi`. - [OpenCode](https://vercel.com/docs/agent-harnesses/opencode): `durable-harness/opencode`. - [fx](https://vercel.com/docs/agent-harnesses/fx): `durable-harness/fx`, libfx's kernel tools for its own durable agents. - [Claude Code](https://vercel.com/docs/agent-harnesses/claude-code) and [Codex](https://vercel.com/docs/agent-harnesses/codex): `durable-harness/claude-code` and `durable-harness/codex`. They run only in the session's own Vercel Sandbox, never in a shared Function ([why](https://vercel.com/docs/agent-harnesses/security)). Model-chosen commands and files run on a virtual workspace (`virtual()`) or in the session's own Vercel Sandbox (`sandbox()`), never on the machine that drives the session. See [tools](https://vercel.com/docs/agent-harnesses/tools) and [security](https://vercel.com/docs/agent-harnesses/security). ## Sending messages A message goes to a session as one of three kinds: `prompt` (the default), `followUp` or `steer` (`sessions.send(sessionId, text, kind)`, or a chat route's POST `kind`). On an idle session, each kind starts a turn. When a message arrives while a turn is running, what happens depends on the harness: | Harness | `steer` during a turn | `prompt` or `followUp` during a turn | | --- | --- | --- | | Pi (`durable-harness/pi-durable` and `durable-harness/pi`) | Goes into the running turn after its current tool calls (Pi's `steer`). | Joins the running turn while Pi is still working on it (Pi's `followUp`). Pi answers it after the turn's own answer, before the turn ends, so the turn's stream carries both answers and ends once. One that arrives as Pi is finishing gets a turn of its own. | | OpenCode | Goes into the running turn at OpenCode's next step. | Waits for the turn to end, then starts its own turn. | | fx | Goes into the running turn at its next model request. | Waits for the turn to end. Messages that waited together then start one turn. | | Claude Code | Goes into the running turn, at priority `next`. | Waits for the turn to end, then starts its own turn. | | Codex | Goes into the running turn (`turn/steer`). If Codex has just ended its turn, the steer runs next, in the same turn. | Waits for the turn to end, then starts its own turn. | On every harness, prompts and follow-ups are answered in the order they were sent, after the turn that was running. The difference is whether a prompt sent during a turn becomes part of that turn, as on Pi, or gets a turn of its own. Pi's agent can only queue mid-turn input as a steer or a follow-up, and Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode take only steers into a running turn. ## Run anywhere Local development uses the Workflow SDK's local World with no configuration. Deploy to Vercel for managed storage, queuing and scaling, with sessions in [Agent Runs](https://vercel.com/docs/agent-harnesses/observability). To self-host, use the Postgres World or any other [World](https://workflow-sdk.dev/docs/deploying): see [self-hosting](https://vercel.com/docs/agent-harnesses/self-hosting). ## Contributing Contributions are welcome. Use [issues](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness/issues) to collaborate with the team, and read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening a pull request. ## Security If you find a security vulnerability in durable-harness, **_disclose it responsibly instead of opening a public issue_**. To participate in our Open Source Software Bug Bounty program, please email [responsible.disclosure@vercel.com](mailto:responsible.disclosure@vercel.com). We will add you to the program and provide further instructions for submitting your report.

# durable-harness

## 0.0.2

### Patch Changes

- [#34](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness/pull/34) [`135dee5`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness/commit/135dee512c6a7aebe710617426c4947c9d2ad498) Thanks [@karthikscale3](https://github.com/karthikscale3)! - Require the latest Workflow SDK v5 Worlds: `@workflow/world` 5.0.5, `@workflow/world-local` 5.1.2, `@workflow/world-vercel` 5.2.3 and `@workflow/world-postgres` 5.0.5.

- [#45](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness/pull/45) [`2ec7587`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness/commit/2ec75874f1c45ef2095aa005782f83d1d80cf151) Thanks [@pranaygp](https://github.com/pranaygp)! - Codex: stop enabling code mode for every model (direct tools need only `direct_only_tool_namespaces`), log calls to tools Codex answers itself, and document what code-mode-only models are offered.

- [#39](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness/pull/39) [`c7d2472`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness/commit/c7d24727bf3c8f64dd73a797b1bc2bed6a653da2) Thanks [@allenzhou101](https://github.com/allenzhou101)! - Expose Codex tools directly for newer models while preserving journal call IDs.

- [#43](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness/pull/43) [`85b564f`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness/commit/85b564f9ba2c61772c205cb9e0a40cce58ee1cbf) Thanks [@pranaygp](https://github.com/pranaygp)! - Read the Gateway's cost from its parsed response metadata, so a cost written in exponent form is charged at its value and a `cost` field elsewhere in the response is ignored.

- [#44](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness/pull/44) [`139e74d`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness/commit/139e74d49347969f7d7ab70976baa190fdd21931) Thanks [@pranaygp](https://github.com/pranaygp)! - Document which Gateway requests `alibaba/qwen3.8-max` on Fireworks refuses for Claude Code, Codex and Pi, and Pi's workaround (set a `thinkingLevel`).

- [#49](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness/pull/49) [`ba45f19`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness/commit/ba45f195442e056873c1c12b2cf084b5afc9ed6a) Thanks [@pranaygp](https://github.com/pranaygp)! - `sandbox({ network })` takes a full Vercel Sandbox `NetworkPolicy` (per-domain rules, including header transforms for credential brokering, and subnets) or a per-session callback, for every harness that runs in a session's Sandbox (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, fx, and pi-durable's `sandboxEnv()`). The harness applies it again on every attach, so set the VM's policy here rather than with `sandbox.update`; header values are kept out of the session's log, its spans, log lines and errors.

- [#50](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness/pull/50) [`62a7ffc`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness/commit/62a7ffc80a3ea20bb8bc8973ca4f5e0e840970dd) Thanks [@pranaygp](https://github.com/pranaygp)! - Document what each harness does with a `prompt`, `followUp` or `steer` sent while a turn runs, and stop `durable-harness/pi` from handing a mid-turn prompt to Pi twice when its inbox is read just before the model call that places it commits.

## 0.0.1

### Patch Changes

- [#10](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness/pull/10) [`9b1ed08`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness/commit/9b1ed08c9ecf5c9a4c6e94db4387f46c8c46c7ae) Thanks [@chadhietala](https://github.com/chadhietala)! - Agent Runs tracing (`agentRuns()` from `/instrumentation/otel`) records sessions with `@vercel/agent-runs@0.0.1`, the library eve uses: a turn per prompt, a step per model call with the tool calls it asks for under it, in the schema Agent Runs reads. A turn that goes on in a later invocation (out of time, a crash, a wake, a lane handoff) stays one turn, its checkpoint kept with the session. A session's `traceAudience` decides what its spans record (`public`: inputs and outputs; anything else: metadata only), and `agentRuns({ capture })` changes that per audience; `exportPolicy` and `filteringProcessor` are removed. Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode record each model request through the Gateway with its prompt, reply and usage.
  
  Recovery applies the current capture policy to restored operations, keeping newly private content out of checkpoints and exports. Recorded tool definitions exclude provider credentials, untraced proxy requests stream without buffering, and tracing failures cannot change agent results. Checkpoint waits are bounded without discarding final updates after a soft budget expires or a write slows down; queued follow-ups retain their own turn identity.
  
  Agent Runs is an optional peer with inlined declaration types. Tracing requires Node.js 24 and optional tracing peers; other entrypoints retain Node.js 22 support.

- [#25](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness/pull/25) [`9f42806`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness/commit/9f42806dc241f3cb0a9b315e3e6f56243e3968ba) Thanks [@pranaygp](https://github.com/pranaygp)! - Explicit CLI help prints to stdout and succeeds at every command level, including sandbox.

- [`0bb39d7`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness/commit/0bb39d7257beaf251473b66f72f0cef0a59bdf2a) Thanks [@pranaygp](https://github.com/pranaygp)! - First release: durable coding-agent harnesses on a Workflow SDK World. Claude Code (`durable-harness/claude-code`), Codex (`/codex`), OpenCode (`/opencode`) and Pi (`/pi`) each run as an agent whose session is a workflow run, its event log the source of truth: every model and tool call is a step in the log, so a crash anywhere resumes the turn from the log on another machine, and a tool that is not safe to rerun comes back to the model as interrupted instead of running twice. Claude Code and Codex run only in the session's own Vercel Sandbox (`workspace: sandbox()`, the default): the CLI runs in a VM per session with the session's Drive at `/workspace`, holds no credential (the Function makes its model calls, within the session's `sandbox({ budget })`), and a session restarted on a new VM keeps its files and resumes from the log. Both are tool-less by default: the app's tools are the only ones the CLI is offered; `builtins: true` turns its own tools on in the VM, each call in the log before it runs. `durable-harness/sandbox` deletes a session's VM and Drive (`deleteSessionSandbox`), cleans up idle ones (`sandboxCleanup`, opt-in), and prepares the base snapshot ahead of time (`npx durable-harness sandbox prepare`); a public chat route for such an agent needs `allowPublicSandbox: true`. OpenCode is tool-less too, starts no process and reads no file of the machine that drives the session for the model, and never changes the process's environment (so it runs beside libfx's agents in one process); `workspace: virtual()` on `opencode()` gives it its own shell, read, write, edit, patch, glob and grep (OpenCode's own tool code, names and schemas) on a virtual workspace, each call's file changes committed with its result, never on the Function's disk (`builtins` narrows them); `workspace: sandbox()` runs the same tools in the session's own Vercel Sandbox, its files on the session's Drive, the VM booted at the first call that needs it. A turn whose installed OpenCode or `effect` isn't the pinned version fails with both versions and the install line. Each agent has a streaming chat route (`agent.chatRoute()`, with an `authorize` check required in production). For apps already built on Pi 1.0's own durable `Harness` (pi-durable), `durable-harness/pi-durable` adds to your code instead of replacing it: open the storage with `openWorldStorage()` where you opened SQLite, JSONL or memory storage, register how a session is reopened with `resumeWith(open)`, and if the process dies mid-turn a wake reopens the session and Pi finishes the turn; `CodingTools` and `env: virtualEnv()` from the same module run Pi 1.0's own coding tools on a virtual workspace, each call's file changes committed with its result, never on the Function's disk, and `env: sandboxEnv()` runs them in the session's own Vercel Sandbox, its files on the session's Drive, armed with the session's own fencing token; a chat route, a shared Harness per session and a read-only follower are optional helpers. `withDurableHarness` (`/next`) sets up the queue's route for Next.js and also serves libfx's durable agents (several, each with its own `name`, with libfx 0.0.14 and later); `/vercel` does the same for Vercel Functions. Self-hosted on world-postgres or world-local, a process that starts the World without making agents (a worker of its own) forwards durable-harness's queue to the app's flow route with `forwardQueue(world)`. Sessions show up in Vercel Agent Runs with their model and tool calls (`agentRuns()` from `/instrumentation/otel`, with OpenTelemetry's SDK installed next to it: optional peers, which nothing else loads), pi-durable's included: a `traceAudience` on `openWorldStorage()` or `resumeWith()` says who sees their content. Pi is tool-less by default; `createCodingTools(virtual())` from `/pi` gives it Pi's own `read`, `bash`, `edit` and `write` (pi-coding-agent's names, schemas and descriptions) on a virtual workspace, or with `createCodingTools(sandbox())` in the session's own Vercel Sandbox (Pi stays in the Function, the VM is attached on the first call), and `pi()` refuses pi-coding-agent's own tools, which run on the host. Also included: documents (typed JSON state per session, `defineDoc`) and example workspace tools (`/tools`) on a virtual workspace (`virtual()`): not real Linux, and nothing of the machine that drives the session (its shell runs in a worker thread leased to that session alone, with an empty environment and a time limit per command), its files in the log, or with `virtual({ durable: false })` in memory for one turn. For libfx's own durable agent (`createFxAgent`), `durable-harness/fx` adds libfx's kernel tools on a virtual workspace (`tools: [...fxTools(virtual())]`): fx's names and schemas, each call's file changes kept with the session and never applied twice; `fxTools(sandbox())` runs them in the session's own Vercel Sandbox, armed with the libfx lease of the worker that runs the call, so a server that was taken over runs nothing more there. Experimental: patch releases only while on 0.0.x.

- [#11](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness/pull/11) [`31c87e8`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness/commit/31c87e8414428fd462dc6ed0853991affd47e0a1) Thanks [@chadhietala](https://github.com/chadhietala)! - libfx's own durable agents show up in Vercel Agent Runs: `createFxAgent({ hooks: agentRunsHooks() })` with `agentRunsHooks` from `durable-harness/fx` records each libfx turn, its steps with their model calls, and its tool calls and the approvals they wait on, from libfx's semantic hooks (libfx 0.0.14 and later). A turn libfx yields, pauses or hands to another worker stays one turn, continued by the execution that resumes it in any process.
  
  Handed-off and fenced turns stay open for recovery; actual user interruption and cancellation finish the turn. Interrupted tool and approval identities are checkpointed so final cleanup also settles recovered calls the engine does not rerun. Execution IDs isolate overlapping deliveries, and ended session bookkeeping is released. Capture follows policy, hook failures use the tracing error handler, and provider/reasoning metadata and turn ordering are preserved. Unawaited hooks and checkpoint flushing remain best-effort.

- [#26](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness/pull/26) [`7b2a18d`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness/commit/7b2a18d04f0476a055a675c86ce81f4331a31ccf) Thanks [@pranaygp](https://github.com/pranaygp)! - Discard interrupted Pi-durable streaming partials before sending their replacement answers on reconnect.

- [#27](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness/pull/27) [`ff32c13`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness/commit/ff32c13368f8a7f24ee939cc8a66c080d51ef10c) Thanks [@pranaygp](https://github.com/pranaygp)! - Pi signals when a recovered reply replaces interrupted streamed text, retaining completed text from the turn.

- [#28](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness/pull/28) [`a5c24a1`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/durable-harness/commit/a5c24a1c5099a31aaf10bced78c400e5a96ce56a) Thanks [@pranaygp](https://github.com/pranaygp)! - Discover exported agents from source syntax without importing scripts or code samples into the generated flow route.
